name: fig_schedule
title: Campaign scheduling: Z3 proposes slots, Lean validSchedule decides
question: Can several experiments be packed into one cooldown of a configuration, where exactly is the feasibility threshold, and does the Lean schedule check catch tampered schedules?
model: Z3 Optimize: start_i >= cooldown, start_i + d_i <= run length, pairwise disjoint, minimise makespan; Lean validSchedule (validSchedule_sound/_bounds/_disjoint/_only_accepted) checks the exact slot list. Durations are user-entered (6, 8, 4, 2 h); cooldown is the documented cooldown_time.max.
data: (a) schedule.schedule_campaign on lakeshore_crx_vf, 48 h, re-run now (paper/data/fig_schedule.json). (b) run-length sweep 16-30 h in 0.5 h steps from paper/data/e6_schedule.json, plus 29 new Lean check_schedule runs on the back-to-back packing. (c) 400 randomly perturbed schedules from paper/data/e6_schedule.json, judged by Lean and by an independent Python re-implementation of ScheduleOK (paper_eval._ok_python).
caption: (a) Lean accepts three experiments on the CRX-VF and Z3 packs them after the 5 h cooldown with a makespan of 23 h; Lean validSchedule accepts the slot list, and the 10 T magnetoresistance experiment is never scheduled because Lean returns DOES NOT MEET for it on this configuration. (b) Z3 finds a schedule exactly from 23 h = cooldown + sum of durations; Lean independently rejects the tightest packing below that and accepts it from 23 h. (c) Of 400 perturbed schedules Lean accepts 139, and agrees with the independent re-implementation on 400/400.
